column1: # EVERY PRODUCTION-REACHABLE, UNMIGRATED C SEMANTIC DECISION IN THE
# SCOPED CORE, PLUS THE EXPLICITLY TESTED EXCLUSIONS.
# A row is a SITE only when it is source-bound, production-reachable
# and makes a semantic decision. A function that is merely a helper,
# a container operation, a diagnostic printer or a DORMANT predicate
# is NOT counted as an authority; the dormant ones are listed in the
# EXCLUSIONS section with the measurement that excluded them.
# REACHABILITY MEASUREMENT: the number of production objects that
# IMPORT the symbol (nm ' U _<sym>'). A static function has internal
# linkage and is reached within its own TU; that is recorded as
# IN_TU. A symbol with zero importers and no in-TU caller is DORMANT.
# THE TESTED EXCLUSIONS. Each exclusion is a MEASUREMENT, not an
# assumption. The exclusion reason is the clause it fails.
# The five EXCL-IR-* type predicates above ARE DEFINED in the production
# object ir-types.c.o, but NO production object IMPORTS them and the
# source grep finds only their own definition and their own header
# declaration. They are DORMANT: they make no decision that can reach
# the emitted assembly, the emitted object or a compiled program's
# behaviour. A dormant predicate therefore fails E04 (it is not a
# semantic decision affecting compilation acceptance, IR/assembly/object
# or runtime behaviour) and E05 (no discriminating compiler witness can
# exist for it). They are NOT candidates.
